title: Snowman Top Hat Cupcakes
shortDescription: Vanilla cupcakes with marshmallow snowman heads and piped scarves, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes turn a marshmallow into a snowman head with a mini fudge cookie top hat. A piped buttercream scarf finishes the look in seconds.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
Orange gel food coloring, small amount
Black gel food coloring, small amount
Red gel food coloring for scarves
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla.
Add flour mix and milk in three batches, alternating. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter into liners and bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes fully on a wire rack before decorating.
Beat 1 cup butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar and cream. Beat until smooth.
Tint a small amount of frosting red for scarves. Keep the rest white.
Pipe a white swirl on each cupcake, leaving room at the top for the snowman.
Press a marshmallow onto each swirl to form the snowman head.
Dot two tiny black dots for eyes and a small orange dab for the nose using melted white chocolate tinted with gel color.
Glue a mini sandwich cookie flat side down onto the marshmallow with a dab of melted white chocolate for the hat.
Pipe a small red zigzag scarf around the base of each marshmallow to finish.
tips: Chill marshmallows for 10 minutes before placing them, they hold their shape better on warm frosting.
Use a toothpick dipped in gel color for tiny dot eyes, it gives more control than a piping tip.
If your kitchen is warm, refrigerate decorated cupcakes for 10 minutes before serving so faces stay put.
Make the scarves with a small star tip for texture that looks like knit fabric.

faq.question: Can I make the snowman heads ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, glue the cookie hats onto marshmallows and add faces up to 2 days ahead. Store them in a single layer in a covered container at room temperature.

faq.question: Why did my marshmallow slide off the frosting?
faq.answer: The frosting swirl was likely too soft or warm. Pipe a firm swirl and chill cupcakes for a few minutes before adding the marshmallow.

faq.question: What can I use instead of mini sandwich cookies for the hat?
faq.answer: A small circle of black fondant on top of a chocolate wafer works as a swap. Any small flat black candy piece will do.

faq.question: Can I use marshmallow fluff instead of a whole marshmallow?
faq.answer: No, this recipe needs a whole marshmallow to form the round snowman head shape. Fluff will not hold its form on top of the cupcake.

conclusion: These snowman cupcakes bring holiday cheer to any dessert table. Kids love helping stick on the marshmallow heads and piping the scarves.
